title: Markdown Editor: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Markdown Editor](/markdown-editor) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Write Markdown and see the formatted result live, side by side. Enter your markdown and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Write Markdown and watch the formatted result appear live beside it — headings, bold and italic text, links, lists, quotes and code, rendered as you type. It is the quick way to draft a README, a blog post or notes without opening a full editor. This is a public writing tool for visitors; it is separate from the site's admin post editor. Everything runs in your browser and nothing you type is saved or uploaded.

## How to use the Markdown Editor

Start by typing or pasting your markdown. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste Markdown in the editor on the left.
2. Read the formatted result in the preview on the right.
3. Copy the Markdown (or the preview) when you are done.

## How it works

The [Markdown Editor](/markdown-editor) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Typing `# Hello` shows a large heading in the preview; `**bold**` shows bold text; `- One` starts a bulleted list. Try the same figures in the [Markdown Editor](/markdown-editor) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Markdown Editor](/markdown-editor) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What Markdown is supported

Headings (#, ##, ###), bold and italic, links (including links to pages on this site), lists, blockquotes, inline code and fenced code blocks, horizontal rules and images. Raw HTML in the input is shown as text, never rendered — the preview is safe by construction.

## Where Markdown is useful

README files, documentation, blog posts, notes and messages on platforms that accept Markdown. It is plain text, so it works in any editor and in version control, and it converts cleanly to HTML when published.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Start a line with # for a heading, - for a bullet, > for a quote.
- Wrap text in ** for bold and * for italic.
- Links look like [text](/bmi-calculator).

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Markdown?

A plain-text way to write formatted documents: # makes a heading, **bold** makes bold text, - makes a list item. It converts to HTML when published. Try it with your own numbers in the [Markdown Editor](/markdown-editor) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is anything I type saved?

No. The editor is a public tool — what you type stays in your browser and is never saved or uploaded. Try it with your own numbers in the [Markdown Editor](/markdown-editor) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is this the same as the site's blog editor?

No. This is a public writing tool for visitors. The site's blog posts are edited in the admin panel, which is a separate editor. Try it with your own numbers in the [Markdown Editor](/markdown-editor) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Markdown Editor?

Just Markdown. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
